name: sync-real-claude-code
description: Sync real Claude Code sessions from ~/.claude into a fresh database
given: User has Claude Code sessions at ~/.claude/projects/
when: Sync runs with claude-code source
then: Sessions indexed with source='claude-code', projects have paths, turns have content
validates: Claude Code adapter discovery + parsing + DB insertion

name: sync-real-codex
description: Sync real Codex sessions from ~/.codex into a fresh database
given: User has Codex sessions at ~/.codex/sessions/
when: Sync runs with codex source
then: Sessions indexed with source='codex'
validates: Codex adapter discovery + parsing + DB insertion

name: multi-source-sync
description: Both Claude Code and Codex sessions sync into one database
given: Both ~/.claude and ~/.codex have sessions
when: Sync runs with both sources configured
then: Both sources present in DB with correct source column values
validates: Multi-source config + sync iteration + source tagging

name: source-filtered-search
description: Search with source: filter returns only matching source
given: Database with sessions from both sources
when: Search with source:codex or source:claude-code
then: Only sessions from the specified source are returned, no cross-contamination
validates: source: query parsing + SQL WHERE clause + source column correctness

name: incremental-sync
description: Second sync skips unchanged files
given: Database already synced from Claude Code sessions
when: Sync runs again with no file changes
then: At most 2 sessions re-synced (active sessions may have changed)
validates: Mtime-based incremental sync with source tracking

name: migration-bootstrap
description: Fresh database gets all migrations applied correctly
given: Empty SQLite database
when: db.Open() creates and migrates the database
then: schema_version at version 3, source column exists with 'claude-code' default
validates: Versioned migration system + migration 003 source columns

name: adapter-registry
description: Registered adapters resolve by type name
given: claudecode, codex, jeff, and hex adapter packages imported
when: adapter.Get() called with known and unknown type names
then: Known types return correct adapters, unknown type returns error
validates: Adapter registry init() registration + Get() lookup

name: backward-compat-config
description: Old-style config auto-creates default source
given: Config file with only claude_home key (no sources)
when: Config loaded via LoadFrom()
then: Single claude-code source auto-created from claude_home path
validates: Backward compatibility for pre-multi-source configs

name: binary-builds
description: Project compiles to a working binary
given: Go source code compiles
when: make build runs
then: ccvault binary exists at project root
validates: No compilation errors across all packages

name: sync-real-jeff
description: Sync real Jeff sessions from ~/.jeff into a fresh database
given: User has Jeff sessions at ~/.jeff/sessions/
when: Sync runs with jeff source
then: Sessions indexed with source='jeff', synthetic project path, turns have content
validates: Jeff adapter discovery + JSONL parsing + turn/tool extraction + DB insertion

name: sync-real-hex
description: Sync real Hex sessions from ~/.hex into a fresh database
given: User has Hex sessions at ~/.hex/sessions/
when: Sync runs with hex source
then: Sessions indexed with source='hex', synthetic project path, turns have content
validates: Hex adapter discovery + JSON parsing + message mapping + DB insertion

name: source-filtered-search-jeff
description: Search with source:jeff returns only Jeff sessions
given: Database with Claude Code and Jeff sessions
when: Search with source:jeff
then: Only Jeff sessions returned, no cross-contamination
validates: source:jeff query parsing + SQL WHERE clause + source column correctness

name: fts-across-sources
description: Full-text search works across multiple sources
given: Multi-source database with indexed content from both sources
when: FTS search for common terms
then: Results returned from the FTS5 index covering both sources
validates: FTS5 triggers fire for all sources, search spans full corpus

name: oversized-jsonl-line-does-not-drop-session
description: A JSONL line larger than 10 MB (e.g. a base64 PDF page) still lets the whole session sync (issue #11)
given: A Claude Code session file has one ~12 MB line surrounded by normal turns
when: ccvault sync runs against the session
then: Session is indexed with all its turns; sync summary reports non-zero 'Truncated raw_json' and does NOT crash with 'token too long'
validates: bufio.Reader-backed parser + line cap + raw_json truncation (#11 fix, PR #12)

name: malformed-only-file-surfaces-skipped-lines
description: A session file containing only malformed JSONL surfaces skipped-line diagnostics instead of vanishing silently
given: A file with zero valid JSONL lines exists in the Claude Code projects dir
when: ccvault sync runs
then: Sync summary reports 'Skipped lines: N across 1 session(s)'; file is counted as SessionsSkipped, not SessionsIndexed; mtime is recorded so subsequent syncs are no-ops
validates: Sync aggregates ParseStats before the empty-session early-return (#12 review fix)

name: raw-json-truncation-persists-to-db
description: For turns whose source line exceeds the 1 MB raw_json threshold, the DB stores a small placeholder instead of the original blob
given: A session with a ~12 MB JSONL line has been synced
when: Query turns.raw_json for the huge turn
then: raw_json is < 500 bytes, has _ccvault_stripped=true, and _ccvault_original_size records the pre-truncation size
validates: strippedRawJSON placeholder + turn.RawJSON reassignment before DB write

name: base64-payload-does-not-pollute-fts
description: Base64 image payloads (PDF pages) do not leak into the FTS5 index because ExtractContent returns "" for image-block tool_results
given: A session with a 12 MB base64 payload has been synced
when: FTS search for a distinctive run of base64 characters
then: Zero results — the payload is not indexed in turns_fts
validates: extractContent behavior on array-shaped tool_result content

name: tool-filter-case-insensitive
description: The tool: search filter matches regardless of case so agents don't have to know the exact capitalization stored in tool_uses
given: A DB where a turn used the tool 'Bash'
when: search runs with 'tool:bash', 'tool:Bash', and 'tool:BASH'
then: All three queries return the same non-empty result set
validates: buildQuery emits 'tu.tool_name = ? COLLATE NOCASE' (PR #10, commit 33df6bf)

name: empty-tool-filter-returns-hint
description: An empty result for a tool: search returns a hint and similar_tool_names so the agent can retry with a closer match
given: A DB containing tool_uses for 'mcp__ccvault__search_conversations'
when: search_conversations is called with tool:ccvault (a fragment that never full-name matches)
then: count=0, hint is non-empty and points at exact-name matching, similar_tool_names surfaces the close match
validates: searchConversations empty-result branch + GetToolNamesLike (PR #10, commits 9bb6b4b + ed46b45)

name: list-sessions-pagination-hint
description: list_sessions and list_projects flag has_more:true with a pagination hint when the caller's limit truncates the result
given: A DB seeded with 3 sessions in one project
when: list_sessions is called with limit=2
then: count=2, has_more=true, and hint is a non-empty string mentioning raising the limit; when limit=100 no has_more field appears
validates: listSessions/listProjects fetch limit+1 + trim + has_more/hint (PR #10, commit 9bb6b4b)

name: orient-warns-on-stat-failure
description: ccvault orient collects stat-query errors into a warnings slice rather than pretending the archive is empty
given: A DB handle whose connection has been closed (every subsequent stat query fails)
when: gatherOrientation runs against that handle
then: Warnings contains one entry per failed query (6 total: project stats, session stats, activity range, tool stats, model stats, recent projects)
validates: gatherOrientation's warn() closure appends on error instead of swallowing (PR #10, commit 93fda15)

name: analytics-unavailable-hint
description: get_analytics returns an explicit availability:false object with a build-cache hint when the DuckDB analytics cache is missing
given: A Server whose analyzer is nil and whose analyzerErr carries the init failure reason
when: getAnalytics is called
then: result.analytics is a map with available=false, reason containing the init error, and hint mentioning 'build-cache'
validates: getAnalytics analyzer==nil fallback branch (PR #10, commit e1dec6d)

name: full-sync-clears-stale-data
description: ccvault sync --full wipes every data table before re-scanning, so projects and sessions that no longer exist upstream are removed from the DB instead of lingering
given: A DB that was previously synced from a source containing project A; A is then removed upstream and replaced by project B
when: sync runs with the full flag against the same source
then: After sync, exactly one project (B) exists in the DB; A's session and project rows have been removed
validates: db.ResetAll() + Syncer.Run() full branch (PR #22)

name: incremental-sync-preserves-stale-rows
description: A normal (non-full) sync does NOT invoke ResetAll — rows for source files that disappear briefly (e.g. an unmounted disk) survive the next sync
given: A DB with one indexed session whose source file has since been removed from disk
when: sync runs without the full flag
then: The stale session row is still present after the run — only --full is destructive
validates: Sync branch guard: ResetAll only when s.full == true (PR #22)

name: display-name-is-basename
description: parser.GetDisplayName returns filepath.Base of the project path, giving CLI/TUI/MCP a short, unambiguous project label; the PATH column beside it provides disambiguation
given: A project path like /Users/harper/Public/src/2389/ccvault
when: GetDisplayName is called on that path
then: Return value is exactly 'ccvault' (the last path component); no ~ substitution, no multi-segment join
validates: scanner.go GetDisplayName basename refactor (PR #22)

name: tui-projects-shows-path-column
description: The TUI Projects list renders a PATH column alongside PROJECT and SOURCE so users can distinguish same-named projects at a glance
given: A DB with two projects whose display names or basenames could collide
when: The Projects TUI model loads and renders its View
then: The rendered string contains the PATH column header and each project's full filesystem path
validates: ProjectsModel.View() header + row layout (PR #22)

name: tui-sessions-conditional-project-column
description: The TUI Sessions list adds a PROJECT column ONLY when it is not filtered to a specific project — when drilled into one project, the redundant column is suppressed
given: A DB with one project and one session
when: The Sessions TUI model renders, first without SetProject then with SetProject(id)
then: Unfiltered view header contains 'PROJECT'; filtered view header starts with 'STARTED' (no PROJECT column)
validates: SessionsModel.View() showProject := m.project == nil branch (PR #22)

name: tui-search-vim-nav-respects-focus
description: vim-style g/G shortcuts only jump the cursor when the search input is unfocused; when the user is typing, g/G go to the input as literal characters
given: A SearchModel with 3 results and cursor at position 2
when: 'G' is dispatched while m.focused == true, then again while m.focused == false
then: Focused: cursor stays at 2 (input consumes G). Unfocused: cursor jumps to len(results)-1. 'g' unfocused jumps to 0
validates: search.go default-case gate on m.focused (PR #22)

name: projectref-class-a-tabular
description: CLI list-projects, TUI Projects/Sessions/Dashboard/Analytics tables render a project label via projectref.Label with the disambiguating PATH shown in its own column
given: A DB with a project whose DisplayName is 'ccvault' and Path is /Users/dyl/work/2389/ccvault
when: The Projects TUI or CLI list-projects renders
then: projectref.Label returns 'ccvault'; PATH column shows the full path (with ~ substitution guarded by separator boundary)
validates: projectref.Label + Class A rendering discipline

name: projectref-class-b-inline
description: CLI search results, orient text bullets, TUI Sessions title (scoped), MCP promptAnalyzeProject header — one-line rows use projectref.Inline for a combined 'name (~/path)' form
given: A project whose DisplayName equals its basename and Path is under HOME
when: projectref.Inline renders it for a Class B surface
then: Output shows the tilde-abbreviated path (or 'name (~/path)' when the adapter provided a non-basename label); never just the bare basename in ambiguous contexts
validates: projectref.Inline + Class B rendering discipline

name: projectref-class-c-structured
description: orient --json, MCP list_projects, MCP session-carrying responses emit projects as {name, path} objects via projectref.Ref — never bare name strings
given: A slice of Project rows in the DB
when: orient --json is serialized (or any MCP response carrying project references)
then: recent_projects (and equivalent MCP fields) is an array of {name, path} objects; both fields always present so agent consumers can disambiguate
validates: projectref.Ref + Class C rendering discipline

name: projectref-class-d-input-matching
description: MCP list_sessions {project:...}, promptAnalyzeProject, and CLI list-sessions --project use projectref.ResolveAll and either return all matches (MCP) or refuse-and-list (CLI) rather than silently picking one
given: A DB with three projects sharing the basename 'ccvault' under different parent directories
when: A caller filters with project:'ccvault'
then: MCP list_sessions returns ambiguous_project_filter=true with matched_projects; MCP promptAnalyzeProject errors listing candidates; CLI list-sessions --project errors listing candidates
validates: projectref.ResolveAll + Class D input-matching discipline

name: projectref-ast-allowlist-enforced
description: Any Go code that reads Project.DisplayName outside the projectref helper package or persistence/adapter code fails the AST allowlist test in CI
given: A source file outside the allowlist reads p.DisplayName
when: go test ./test/integration/... runs
then: TestProjectRefEnforcement fails with a specific line reference, preventing the drift class of bug where new surfaces bypass the four-class discipline
validates: test/integration/projectref_allowlist_test.go

name: list-projects-sort-tiebreaker
description: list_projects sort orders that could collide (e.g. name sort with two projects sharing a basename) fall back to path ASC as tiebreaker so results are stable across calls and pagination stays coherent
given: A DB with two projects sharing display_name='ccvault' at different paths
when: list_projects orderBy=name is called twice
then: Both calls return the two rows in the same order (path-ASC secondary sort), stable across pagination
validates: internal/db GetProjects secondary path ASC sort (follow-up 7)

name: compact-path-progressive-initialing
description: compact.Path shortens paths by progressively initialing intermediate segments left-to-right, preserving the last segment as long as possible, before falling back to '…'+tail truncation
given: A path /Users/testuser/work/2389/ccvault under HOME
when: compact.Path is called at successively tighter maxWidths
then: At 20 cols returns ~/work/2389/ccvault (Shortened=false); at 16 returns ~/w/2389/ccvault (Shortened=true); at 13 returns ~/w/2/ccvault; at 4 falls back to visible '…' truncation
validates: internal/compact Path ladder (follow-up 8)

name: compact-model-never-drops-datestamp
description: compact.Model refuses to silently drop a trailing datestamp because opus-4-5-20251101 is a semantically distinct model from opus-4-5; under pressure it end-truncates visibly with '…' instead
given: Model claude-opus-4-5-20251101
when: compact.Model is called with maxWidth 8
then: Result.Text ends with '…' (visible truncation), does NOT equal 'opus-4-5' (which would conflate distinct models), Shortened=true
validates: internal/compact Model correctness — semantic identity preserved over aggressive compaction (follow-up 8)

name: compact-source-ladder
description: compact.Source uses well-known adapter shorthands (claude-code → claude → cc, nanoclaw → nano → nc); unknown adapters end-truncate with '…' to avoid silent mis-mapping
given: Sources 'claude-code' and 'some-unknown-adapter'
when: compact.Source is called at maxWidth 8 for both
then: claude-code returns 'claude' (Shortened=true); unknown adapter returns a '…'-suffixed truncation, never a mis-mapped shorthand
validates: internal/compact Source ladder (follow-up 8)

name: compact-shortened-signals-tui-cell-style
description: Every compact.Result carries Shortened=true when the value was abbreviated; the TUI applies a faint style to those cells so users see at-a-glance that a column has more content behind it
given: A Result with Shortened=true
when: cellText renders it into a padded cell
then: The rendered string is wrapped in compactStyle (lipgloss Faint), while a non-Shortened Result renders as normal text
validates: internal/tui/layout.go cellText + compactStyle in styles.go

name: tui-projects-fits-at-80-cols
description: The TUI Projects list must not overflow an 80-column terminal — pickProjectsLayout drops SOURCE and tightens PATH/PROJECT columns so the widest row stays within budget
given: A DB with a project whose path has 6+ segments
when: m.SetSize(80, 30) is called and View() renders
then: The widest visible row (ignoring ANSI escapes) is ≤ 80 columns; the layout has dropped or shrunk the SOURCE column and initialed intermediate path segments
validates: internal/tui/layout.go pickProjectsLayout + compact.Path

name: tui-shows-full-form-when-roomy
description: Compaction only fires under pressure — at a wide terminal, TUI models render the fullest form (no unnecessary initialing, no compact style)
given: A DB with a project whose path fits within the tier-0 PATH budget
when: m.SetSize(140, 30) is called and View() renders
then: The full path appears verbatim in the rendered view; no cell is styled as compacted
validates: internal/tui/layout.go tier 0 layout + compact.Path natural-form-first
